text:
maria: Heads-up, I'm prototyping a small OTEL "shim" for inference runtimes (py/go/rust). Hit two problems: exporter init blocking during cold start, and inconsistent resource attrs across languages.

aj: can you share examples of the blocking init? we saw similar with the Java SDK a while back.

maria: python example — sync OTLP exporter created on import causes process to hang on startup under low-memory CI:```python
from opentelemetry import trace
from opentelemetry.exporter.otlp.proto.grpc.trace_exporter import OTLPSpanExporter
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import TracerProvider
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export import BatchSpanProcessor

tracer_provider = TracerProvider()
exporter = OTLPSpanExporter(endpoint=os.environ.get('OTLP_ENDPOINT'))
tracer_provider.add_span_processor(BatchSpanProcessor(exporter))
trace.set_tracer_provider(tracer_provider)
```

linh: yeah that's the classic sync ctor issue. we wrap exporter creation in an async initializer + backoff in some services. also make exporter lazy and write to local queue first.

sasha: for Go we did something similar: initialize a buffered channel for OTLP payloads and start the exporter goroutine after startup probes pass. keeps start fast.

tim: +1 on lazy init. also we should standardize resource attributes: `service.name`, `deployment.environment`, `model.name`, `model.variant`, `model.size`, `runtime` (py/go/rust), and `dedicated=true|false`. console relies on these.

maria: agreed. proposal: add small runtime shim per language that normalizes attrs and exposes a single `init_inference_telemetry(config)` call for services. shim responsibilities: lazy exporter init, deterministic span names, KV-cache span hooks, and token/byte attrs.

aj: about sampling: we should be aggressive at ingest time for short low-cost requests. maybe tail-sample everything that errors or exceeds 200ms and sample 1% of fast ones. this lowers retention while keeping anomaly coverage.

linh: tail-sampling needs correlating traces — easier if we add a `trace.events` log export of error spikes to metrics so the collector can pull. but OTEL collector config becomes more complex. are we ok leaning on a sidecar collector?

sasha: sidecar collector + persistent queue in front works well. sidecars can have local retention and retry. for private deployments we default to `local-collector` and for hosted we route to centralized collector cluster.

maria: decision request: 1) build shims (py/go/rust) with lazy exporter + attribute normalization, 2) default to OTLP/grpc w/ BatchSpanProcessor tuned for low-latency inference (max_queue_size small, schedule_delay_ms short), 3) sampling: 100% errors, 10% slow (>200ms), 1% fast otherwise. ok?

aj: +1 from infra, but add config override per-customer and per-route.

tim: +1, add a `kv_cache.hit` boolean attribute on inference spans and emit span events for cache fills/evictions. that will help Optimize dashboards.

linh: implementation notes: go shim will use `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace` with `NewBatchSpanProcessor(exporter, sdktrace.WithMaxExportBatchSize(64), sdktrace.WithScheduleDelayMillis(50))`. python will use our async wrapper for OTLP exporter. rust — we can wrap `opentelemetry-otlp` with tokio task. I'll open PRs.

sasha: UX ask for Console: add a per-model trace funnel widget (error rate, p50/p95 latency from spans) and sample-explorer for traces retained. that'll need new endpoints from telemetry pipeline.

maria: noted — I'll add telemetry API contract to the infra API board.

infra-bot: deploy-cue: created ticket INFRA-4278 for OTEL shims + collector routing. assignees: @linh, @maria.

aj: one more: ensure our shims avoid leaking PII in attributes — strip prompt text by default and only send prompt hashes or lengths.

maria: good call. default: no raw prompt, add `prompt.sha256` and `prompt.length` as attributes. anyone opposed?

all: :thumbsup:

maria: I'll push an RFC doc and PR sketches today. will loop in devex for examples and runtime packaging. thanks all.
